166	
167	Notwithstanding the foregoing exclusions set forth in this Section IV, if an excluded cause of loss as set forth in Sections IV.A through IV.K results in a Covered Cause of Loss, this Policy covers the loss or damage caused by that Covered Cause of Loss. By way of example, if an excluded cause of loss results in a fire, explosion, or other Covered Cause of Loss, the direct physical loss or damage caused by such fire, explosion, or other Covered Cause of Loss is covered under this Policy, subject to all other applicable terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations. This provision shall apply regardless of the sequence of events or the number of intervening causes between the excluded cause of loss and the resulting Covered Cause of Loss, provided that the Covered Cause of Loss is a natural and reasonably foreseeable consequence of the excluded cause of loss. The purpose of this provision is to ensure that the Named Insured is not deprived of coverage for otherwise-covered perils merely because such perils were set in motion by an excluded cause of loss.
168	
169	**[SECTION V --- CONDITIONS]{.underline}**
170	
171	The following conditions apply to all coverages under this Policy. Failure to comply with these conditions may result in the denial or reduction of coverage as provided herein.
172	
173	**[Section V.A --- Notice of Loss]{.underline}**
174	
175	In the event of loss or damage to Covered Property, the Named Insured shall:
176	
177	> \(a\) give notice of such loss or damage to the Insurer as soon as practicable, but in no event later than sixty (60) days after the Named Insured first becomes aware of the loss or damage. Such notice may be given by telephone, electronic mail, or in writing, and shall include the date of loss, a brief description of the nature and extent of the loss or damage, and the Covered Location at which the loss or damage occurred;
178	>
179	> \(b\) protect the Covered Property from further damage and make reasonable and necessary repairs to protect such property. The cost of such protective measures shall be recoverable under this Policy to the extent they are reasonable and necessary, subject to the Limits of Liability;
180	>
181	> \(c\) cooperate with the Insurer in the investigation and adjustment of any claim, including providing access to the Covered Location, making personnel available for interviews, and providing documents and records as reasonably requested by the Insurer; and
182	>
183	> \(d\) submit to the Insurer a signed, sworn proof of loss within ninety (90) days after the date of loss, containing the information required by the Insurer to adjust the claim, including a detailed description of the loss or damage, an estimate of the amount of the claim, and supporting documentation, unless such time is extended by the Insurer in writing.
184	
185	The obligations set forth in subsections (a) and (d) above are separate and distinct requirements with separate deadlines. Compliance with subsection (a) (notice of loss) does not satisfy the requirement of subsection (d) (sworn proof of loss), and compliance with subsection (d) does not excuse non-compliance with subsection (a). 186	
187	**[Section V.B --- Duties After Loss]{.underline}**
188	
189	The Named Insured shall, upon request by the Insurer:
190	
191	> \(a\) provide complete inventories of damaged and undamaged property, showing in detail the quantities, costs, actual cash values, and amounts of loss claimed;
192	>
193	> \(b\) permit the Insurer to inspect the property and examine the Named Insured\'s books and records relating to the Covered Property and the claim, at such reasonable times and places as the Insurer may designate;
194	>
195	> \(c\) submit to examination under oath by any person designated by the Insurer regarding any matter relating to the claim, the loss or damage, or the Named Insured\'s compliance with the terms and conditions of this Policy; and
196	>
197	> \(d\) produce for examination at such reasonable time and place as may be designated by the Insurer, all books, records, bills, invoices, receipts, and other documents, including electronically stored information, relating to the claim or the Covered Property.
198	
199	**[Section V.C --- Subrogation]{.underline}**
200	
201	If the Insurer pays or agrees to pay any claim under this Policy, the Insurer shall be subrogated to all of the Named Insured\'s rights of recovery against any person or entity with respect to such claim. The Named Insured shall execute and deliver such instruments and papers and do whatever else is necessary to secure such rights. The Named Insured shall not do anything after loss to prejudice such rights.
202	
203	**[Section V.D --- Other Insurance]{.underline}**
204	
205	If there is other valid and collectible insurance covering the same loss or damage as is covered under this Policy, this Policy shall apply as excess insurance and shall not contribute with such other insurance. The Named Insured shall disclose to the Insurer the existence of any other insurance that may cover a loss or damage that is also covered under this Policy.
206	
207	**[Section V.E --- Suit Against Insurer]{.underline}**
208	
209	No suit, action, or proceeding shall be brought against the Insurer for recovery under this Policy unless the Named Insured has fully complied with all of the terms of this Policy and unless such suit, action, or proceeding is commenced within two (2) years after the date of the loss or damage giving rise to the claim. If applicable law provides a longer limitations period, the provisions of applicable law shall control.
210	
211	**[Section V.F --- Liberalization]{.underline}**
212	
213	If during the Policy Period the Insurer adopts any revision to this Policy form that would broaden the coverage afforded under this Policy without additional premium charge, such broadened coverage shall immediately apply to this Policy.
214	
215	**[SECTION VI --- BUSINESS INTERRUPTION COVERAGE]{.underline}**
216	
217	**[Section VI.A --- Business Interruption Insuring Agreement]{.underline}**
218	
219	Subject to the terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations of this Policy, including the applicable Limit of Liability and Waiting Period, the Insurer agrees to pay for the actual Business Interruption Loss sustained by the Named Insured during the Period of Restoration resulting from the necessary interruption of the Named Insured\'s business operations caused by direct physical loss of or damage to Covered Property at a Covered Location from a Covered Cause of Loss occurring during the Policy Period. Coverage for Business Interruption Loss is derivative of and dependent upon a finding that the underlying direct physical loss of or damage to Covered Property is covered under this Policy. To the extent that direct physical loss of or damage to Covered Property is covered under Section I of this Policy, including by operation of the Ensuing Loss Provision set forth in the final paragraph of Section IV, the Business Interruption Loss resulting from such covered loss or damage shall likewise be covered under this Section VI.
220	
221	**[Section VI.B --- Business Interruption Loss Defined]{.underline}**
222	
223	\"Business Interruption Loss\" means the actual loss of net income (net profit or loss before income taxes) that would have been earned or incurred by the Named Insured during the Period of Restoration, plus continuing normal operating expenses incurred, including payroll, to the extent such expenses must necessarily continue during the Period of Restoration, less any variable costs and expenses that do not continue during the Period of Restoration. The calculation of Business Interruption Loss shall be based upon the Named Insured\'s historical financial records, including but not limited to income statements, profit and loss statements, and tax returns for the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the date of loss, adjusted for any trends or circumstances that would have affected the Named Insured\'s net income had the loss not occurred.
224	
225	**[Section VI.C --- Period of Restoration]{.underline}**
226	
227	\"Period of Restoration\" means the period of time beginning seventy-two (72) hours after the date of direct physical loss or damage to Covered Property from a Covered Cause of Loss and ending on the earlier of:
228	
229	> \(a\) the date when the Covered Property should be repaired, rebuilt, or replaced with reasonable speed and similar quality; or
230	>
231	> \(b\) the date when business operations are resumed at the Covered Location at the level that would have existed had no loss or damage occurred.
232	
233	The Period of Restoration does not include any increase in the period of restoration caused by the enforcement of any ordinance, law, or regulation that restricts or prohibits the repair, rebuilding, or replacement of Covered Property, unless Ordinance or Law coverage is separately provided under this Policy. The determination of when Covered Property \"should be\" repaired, rebuilt, or replaced with reasonable speed shall take into account the availability of materials, labor, and equipment, as well as any governmental permitting or regulatory requirements that must be satisfied before such repair, rebuilding, or replacement can be completed.
234	
235	**[Section VI.D --- Limit of Liability --- Business Interruption]{.underline}**
236	
237	The Insurer\'s maximum liability for Business Interruption Loss arising out of any one Occurrence shall not exceed Fifteen Million Dollars (\$15,000,000). The Business Interruption Limit of Liability is separate from and in addition to the Property Damage Limit of Liability stated in Section III.A of this Policy. The aggregate of all Business Interruption Loss payments under this Policy for any one Occurrence shall not exceed this Limit of Liability.
238	
239	**[Section VI.E --- Waiting Period]{.underline}**
240	
241	A Waiting Period of seventy-two (72) hours shall apply to each Occurrence for Business Interruption Loss. No Business Interruption Loss shall be payable for the first seventy-two (72) hours of the Period of Restoration. After the expiration of the seventy-two (72) hour Waiting Period, Business Interruption Loss shall be payable from the seventy-third (73rd) hour of the Period of Restoration forward. The Deductible stated in Section III.B of this Policy does not apply to Business Interruption Loss. The Waiting Period set forth in this Section VI.E is the sole threshold applicable to Business Interruption Loss and operates in lieu of the Deductible.
242	
243	**[Section VI.F --- Duty to Mitigate]{.underline}**
244	
245	The Named Insured shall use due diligence and dispatch and do and concur in doing all things reasonably practicable to minimize the Business Interruption Loss. If the Named Insured could reduce the Business Interruption Loss by:
246	
247	> \(a\) making use of other property or facilities owned or available to the Named Insured;
248	>
249	> \(b\) resuming operations of the business, in whole or in part, by using damaged or undamaged property at the Covered Location or elsewhere; or
250	>
251	> \(c\) making use of stock, raw materials, or merchandise at any other location;
252	
253	then any reduction in Business Interruption Loss that could be reasonably achieved shall be taken into account in determining the amount payable under this Section VI. The Named Insured\'s obligation under this provision is one of reasonableness and does not require the Named Insured to undertake extraordinary measures, incur unreasonable expense, or resume operations in a manner that would expose employees, the public, or the environment to undue risk. The standard for determining whether Business Interruption Loss could have been reduced shall be what a reasonable and prudent operator of a similar business would have done under the same or similar circumstances, taking into account the nature and extent of the damage, applicable regulatory requirements, and the availability of alternative facilities, equipment, and materials. Any amounts expended by the Named Insured in reasonable efforts to mitigate Business Interruption Loss shall be recoverable under this Policy as part of the Business Interruption Loss, to the extent such amounts reduce the overall Business Interruption Loss that would otherwise have been sustained.
254	
255	**[Section VI.G --- Exclusions Applicable to Business Interruption Coverage]{.underline}**
256	
257	Business Interruption Loss is subject to the same exclusions stated in Section IV of this Policy. Any loss or damage to Covered Property that is excluded under Section IV shall not give rise to a Business Interruption Loss payable under this Section VI. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Ensuing Loss Provision set forth in the final paragraph of Section IV shall apply equally to claims for Business Interruption Loss under this Section VI. Accordingly, if an excluded cause of loss results in a Covered Cause of Loss that causes direct physical loss of or damage to Covered Property, and such loss or damage results in a necessary interruption of business operations, the resulting Business Interruption Loss shall be covered under this Section VI, subject to the Waiting Period, Limit of Liability, and all other applicable terms and conditions.

**[DECLARATIONS PAGE]{.underline}**

**PINNACLE ASSURANCE CORPORATION** 400 Commerce Tower, Hartford, CT 06103

**POLLUTION LEGAL LIABILITY POLICY**

**[SECTION I --- INSURING AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**I.A --- Coverage Grant**

Subject to all terms, conditions, limitations, and exclusions of this Policy, the Insurer agrees to pay on behalf of the Insured those Remediation Costs and Claim Expenses that the Insured becomes legally obligated to pay as a result of a Claim first made against the Insured and reported to the Insurer during the Policy Period, or any applicable Extended Reporting Period, arising from a Pollution Condition at, on, under, or migrating from a Covered Location, provided that: (1) the Claim is first made against the Insured during the Policy Period or any applicable Extended Reporting Period; (2) the Claim is reported in writing to the Insurer in accordance with Section IV.A of this Policy; and (3) the Pollution Condition giving rise to the Claim first commences on or after the Retroactive Date stated in the Declarations. Coverage under this Policy shall apply only to Claims first made and reported during the Policy Period. There shall be no coverage under this Policy for any Claim first made prior to the inception of the Policy Period or after the expiration of the Policy Period, except as may be provided under an Extended Reporting Period endorsement.

**I.B --- Defense Obligation**

The Insurer shall have the right and duty to defend any Claim to which this insurance applies, even if any of the allegations of the Claim are groundless, false, or fraudulent. The Insurer shall have the right to appoint defense counsel of its choosing. Defense Costs shall be included within and shall reduce the applicable Limit of Liability as set forth in Section VI of this Policy. The Insurer\'s obligation to defend shall cease upon exhaustion of the applicable Limit of Liability.

**I.C --- Duty to Cooperate**

The Insured shall cooperate with the Insurer in the investigation, defense, and settlement of any Claim. The Insured shall not, except at the Insured\'s own cost, voluntarily make any payment, assume any obligation, or incur any expense without the prior written consent of the Insurer, other than reasonable emergency response expenses necessarily incurred to prevent imminent harm to human health or the environment.

*\[Sections I.D through I.F omitted\]*

**[SECTION II --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Policy, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Defined terms appear in this Policy with initial capitalization. Where the context requires, the singular shall include the plural and the plural shall include the singular.

**II.A --- \"Claim\"**

\"Claim\" means: (1) a written demand received by the Insured seeking Remediation Costs, damages, or other relief arising from a Pollution Condition; (2) a civil proceeding commenced by the filing of a complaint or similar pleading against the Insured seeking Remediation Costs, damages, or other relief arising from a Pollution Condition; or (3) a governmental or regulatory directive, order, notice, or request that the Insured investigate, remove, remediate, or otherwise respond to a Pollution Condition, including but not limited to any compliance order, consent decree, notice of violation, enforcement action, or administrative order issued by a federal, state, or local governmental authority. A Claim shall be deemed to have been first made on the date on which the Insured first receives the written demand, complaint, pleading, directive, order, notice, or request described above.

**II.B --- \"Claim Expenses\"**

\"Claim Expenses\" means reasonable and necessary fees, costs, and expenses incurred by the Insurer, or by the Insured with the Insurer\'s prior written consent, in the investigation, adjustment, defense, or appeal of a Claim, including but not limited to attorneys\' fees, expert witness fees, consultant fees, court costs, and costs of depositions and transcripts. Claim Expenses shall not include any salary, wages, overhead, or benefit expenses of the Insured, or any amounts incurred by the Insured prior to the Insurer\'s written acknowledgment of a Claim under this Policy except as otherwise expressly provided herein.

*\[Sections II.C through II.F omitted\]*

**II.G --- \"Covered Location\"**

\"Covered Location\" means any location listed on Schedule A attached to and forming part of this Policy, as such Schedule A may be amended by endorsement during the Policy Period. The term Covered Location shall include all buildings, structures, tanks, equipment, appurtenances, and land areas within the property boundaries of the locations so described.

*\[Sections II.H through II.L omitted\]*

**II.M --- \"Insured\"**

\"Insured\" means: (1) the Named Insured designated in the Declarations; (2) any Subsidiary of the Named Insured, as defined in this Policy; and (3) any past, present, or future director, officer, or employee of the Named Insured or its Subsidiary, but only while acting within the scope of their duties as such. The term Insured shall not include any independent contractor, consultant, or agent of the Named Insured unless specifically added by endorsement.

**II.N --- \"Pollution Condition\"**

\"Pollution Condition\" means the discharge, dispersal, release, or escape of any Pollutants into or upon land, the atmosphere, or any watercourse or body of water, including groundwater. The term Pollution Condition shall include the presence of Pollutants in or on any environmental media, including but not limited to soil, surface water, groundwater, sediment, or ambient air, resulting from such discharge, dispersal, release, or escape. A Pollution Condition shall not include the mere presence of a substance within a contained vessel, tank, or piping system, provided that no discharge, dispersal, release, or escape of Pollutants from such vessel, tank, or piping system has occurred. The existence of a structural deficiency, corrosion, wear, or deterioration of any vessel, tank, or piping system shall not, in and of itself, constitute a Pollution Condition absent an actual discharge, dispersal, release, or escape of Pollutants therefrom.

**II.O --- \"Pollutant\" / \"Pollutants\"**

\"Pollutant\" or \"Pollutants\" means any solid, liquid, gaseous, or thermal irritant, contaminant, or toxic or hazardous substance, including but not limited to smoke, vapor, soot, fumes, acids, alkalis, chemicals, or waste. The term Pollutant includes but is not limited to any substance designated as hazardous or toxic under any applicable federal, state, or local environmental law, regulation, or ordinance, and any materials which require investigation, removal, remediation, or other response action under any such law, regulation, or ordinance. The term Pollutant also includes any substance that, when discharged, dispersed, released, or escaped into or upon environmental media, causes or threatens to cause contamination, degradation, or impairment of such environmental media. The characterization of a substance as a \"standard,\" \"common,\" or \"industrial\" chemical or material shall not, in and of itself, preclude such substance from being considered a Pollutant under this Policy.

**II.P --- \"Remediation Costs\"**

\"Remediation Costs\" means reasonable and necessary expenses incurred to investigate, quantify, monitor, mitigate, abate, remove, dispose of, treat, neutralize, or immobilize Pollutants in or on environmental media at, on, under, or migrating from a Covered Location, including but not limited to costs for site assessments, remedial investigations, feasibility studies, remedial design, remedial action, soil excavation and disposal, groundwater monitoring and treatment, vapor intrusion assessment and mitigation, regulatory compliance activities, and costs incurred in connection with the preparation of reports, plans, and submissions required by governmental authorities. Remediation Costs shall not include costs for the repair, replacement, or restoration of any tank, vessel, structure, or equipment, except to the extent that such repair, replacement, or restoration is required as a component of an approved remedial action plan directed at the abatement of a Pollution Condition.

*\[Sections II.Q through II.T omitted\]*

**[SECTION III --- COVERAGE TERRITORY]{.underline}**

**III.A --- Territory**

This Policy applies to Pollution Conditions at Covered Locations within the United States of America, its territories, and possessions.

*\[Remainder of Section III omitted\]*

**[SECTION IV --- CONDITIONS]{.underline}**

**IV.A --- Notice of Claim**

As a condition precedent to coverage under this Policy, the Insured shall provide written notice to the Insurer of any Claim as soon as practicable after the Insured first becomes aware of the Claim, but in no event later than ninety (90) days after the end of the Policy Period or any applicable Extended Reporting Period. Such notice shall be provided to the Insurer at the following address:

> Pinnacle Assurance Corporation Claims Department 400 Commerce Tower Hartford, CT 06103

or by electronic mail to claims@pinnacleassurance.com.

Notice shall include: (1) the specific Covered Location involved; (2) a description of the Pollution Condition giving rise to the Claim; (3) the identity of any governmental authority or third party making the Claim; (4) copies of any written demands, complaints, orders, directives, or other documents received by the Insured relating to the Claim; and (5) a preliminary estimate of the Remediation Costs and Claim Expenses anticipated in connection with the Claim. The Insured\'s failure to provide timely notice as required under this Section IV.A shall relieve the Insurer of any obligation under this Policy with respect to the Claim for which notice was required, to the extent permitted by applicable law.

**IV.B --- Insured\'s Duties Upon a Claim**

Upon becoming aware of a Claim or a potential Claim under this Policy, the Insured shall:

> \(a\) cooperate fully with the Insurer and its authorized representatives in the investigation, defense, and settlement of the Claim;
>
> \(b\) not voluntarily admit liability, make any payment, assume any obligation, or incur any expense (except for reasonable and necessary emergency response costs to prevent imminent harm to human health or the environment) without the prior written consent of the Insurer;
>
> \(c\) promptly forward to the Insurer copies of all demands, notices, summonses, complaints, orders, directives, and other legal papers and documents received in connection with the Claim;
>
> \(d\) provide the Insurer with such information, documentation, and cooperation as the Insurer may reasonably request, including but not limited to authorizations for the release of records and information;
>
> \(e\) take all reasonable measures to mitigate or prevent the further discharge, dispersal, release, or escape of Pollutants from a Covered Location upon discovery of a Pollution Condition; and
>
> \(f\) not take any action that would impair, prejudice, or waive the Insurer\'s rights of subrogation under Section VII.D of this Policy.

The Insured\'s failure to comply with the duties set forth in this Section IV.B shall not relieve the Insurer of its obligations under this Policy unless such failure materially prejudices the Insurer\'s rights or interests, to the extent permitted by applicable law.

*\[Sections IV.C through IV.H omitted\]*

**[SECTION V --- EXCLUSIONS]{.underline}**

This Policy does not apply to, and the Insurer shall have no obligation to pay any Remediation Costs, Claim Expenses, or other amounts in connection with:

**V.A --- Bodily Injury and Property Damage to Third Parties**

Bodily injury or property damage to third parties, except to the extent that such bodily injury or property damage arises directly from a Pollution Condition at a Covered Location and is inseparable from the Remediation Costs covered under this Policy. This exclusion shall not apply to diminution in property value resulting from a Pollution Condition at a Covered Location to the extent such diminution is otherwise covered under this Policy.

*\[Section V.B omitted\]*

**V.C --- Known Conditions**

Any Pollution Condition which existed prior to the inception of this Policy and which was known to the Insured prior to the inception of this Policy. For purposes of this exclusion, a Pollution Condition shall be deemed \"known to the Insured\" if any officer, director, general counsel, risk manager, environmental manager, or facility manager of the Named Insured was aware, as of the inception date of this Policy, of facts or circumstances that would lead a reasonable person to conclude that a Pollution Condition, as defined in Section II.N of this Policy, existed at a Covered Location. The knowledge of any other employee, agent, or representative of the Insured shall not be imputed to the Insured for purposes of this exclusion. For the avoidance of doubt, knowledge of a structural deficiency, maintenance condition, or physical state of a vessel, tank, piping system, or other equipment at a Covered Location shall not constitute knowledge of a Pollution Condition under this exclusion unless such knowledge includes awareness of an actual or ongoing discharge, dispersal, release, or escape of Pollutants, as those terms are defined in this Policy.

*\[Sections V.D and V.E omitted\]*

**V.F --- Intentional Non-Compliance**

Any Pollution Condition resulting from the Insured\'s intentional non-compliance with any statute, regulation, ordinance, or governmental directive applicable to the prevention, control, abatement, or remediation of Pollutants at a Covered Location. For purposes of this exclusion, \"intentional non-compliance\" means the Insured\'s knowing and willful failure to comply with a specific requirement of an applicable statute, regulation, ordinance, or governmental directive, where the Insured had actual knowledge of such requirement and consciously chose not to comply. This exclusion shall not apply to the Insured\'s failure to comply with industry standards, recommended practices, voluntary codes of conduct, or guidelines that do not have the force of law unless such standards, practices, codes, or guidelines have been expressly adopted and incorporated into an applicable statute, regulation, ordinance, or governmental directive by the relevant governmental authority.

**V.G --- Criminal Acts and Fraud**

Any Pollution Condition resulting from any criminal act, fraud, or intentional misconduct by or at the direction of the Insured, as established by a final adjudication in a court of competent jurisdiction or by the Insured\'s written admission. This exclusion shall not apply to bar defense of a Claim until such final adjudication or admission has been obtained.

**V.H --- Contractual Liability**

Any liability assumed by the Insured under any contract or agreement, except to the extent that the Insured would have been liable for such Remediation Costs or Claim Expenses in the absence of such contract or agreement.

*\[Sections V.I through V.K omitted\]*

**[SECTION VI --- LIMIT OF LIABILITY AND SELF-INSURED RETENTION]{.underline}**

**VI.A --- Per-Claim Limit**

The Insurer\'s maximum liability for all Remediation Costs and Claim Expenses arising from any single Claim shall not exceed the Per-Claim Limit of Liability stated in the Declarations, which is Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000). Claim Expenses, including but not limited to defense costs, shall be included within and shall reduce the Per-Claim Limit of Liability. Once the Per-Claim Limit of Liability has been exhausted by the payment of Remediation Costs and Claim Expenses, the Insurer shall have no further obligation to pay any Remediation Costs or Claim Expenses, or to defend any Claim, with respect to such Claim.

**VI.B --- Aggregate Limit**

The Insurer\'s maximum liability for all Remediation Costs and Claim Expenses arising from all Claims during the Policy Period shall not exceed the Aggregate Limit of Liability stated in the Declarations, which is Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000), regardless of the number of Claims, Pollution Conditions, or Covered Locations involved. Once the Aggregate Limit of Liability has been exhausted, the Insurer shall have no further obligation under this Policy for the remainder of the Policy Period.

**VI.C --- Self-Insured Retention**

The Insured shall be responsible for the payment of the Self-Insured Retention stated in the Declarations, which is One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$150,000), for each Claim. The Self-Insured Retention shall apply to Remediation Costs and Claim Expenses combined. The Insurer\'s obligation to pay Remediation Costs and Claim Expenses shall attach only after the Insured has satisfied the Self-Insured Retention for the applicable Claim. Payment of the Self-Insured Retention by the Insured shall be a condition precedent to the Insurer\'s obligation to pay any amounts under this Policy with respect to such Claim. The Self-Insured Retention shall not reduce the applicable Limit of Liability.

**VI.D --- Related Claims**

All Claims arising from the same, related, or continuous Pollution Condition shall be deemed a single Claim for purposes of this Policy, and such single Claim shall be deemed first made on the date the earliest of such Claims was first made against the Insured. A single Per-Claim Limit of Liability and a single Self-Insured Retention shall apply to all such related Claims.

**[SECTION VII --- GENERAL CONDITIONS]{.underline}**

**(Excerpted).**

**VII.A --- Entire Agreement**

This Policy, including the Declarations, Schedule(s), and all endorsements attached hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the Insured and the Insurer with respect to the insurance provided hereunder. No change, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Policy shall be valid unless made by written endorsement issued by the Insurer and attached to this Policy. No agent, broker, or other representative of the Insured has authority to change, modify, or waive any provision of this Policy.

**VII.B --- Governing Law**

This Policy shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the state in which the Covered Location giving rise to the Claim is situated, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. In the event that a Claim involves multiple Covered Locations in different states, the law of the state in which the first Covered Location is listed on Schedule A shall govern.

**VII.C --- Assignment**

The interest of the Insured under this Policy shall not be assigned, transferred, or conveyed without the prior written consent of the Insurer. Any assignment, transfer, or conveyance without such consent shall be void and of no effect.

**VII.D --- Subrogation**

In the event of any payment under this Policy, the Insurer shall be subrogated to all rights of recovery of the Insured against any person or entity responsible for the Pollution Condition giving rise to such payment. The Insured shall execute and deliver such instruments and papers and shall do whatever else is necessary to secure and preserve such rights. The Insured shall not take any action after a loss to impair or prejudice the Insurer\'s rights of subrogation.

31	**[Section 1 --- Assignment and Scope of Investigation]{.underline}**
32	
33	Vector Engineering Solutions, LLC (\"Vector\") was retained by Pinnacle Assurance Corporation (\"Pinnacle\") on March 20, 2025, through Crossfield Adjusting Group, LLC (\"Crossfield\"), to conduct a forensic engineering investigation into the catastrophic failure of Tank 7 and the subsequent fire and explosion at the Greenfield Specialty Chemicals, Inc. (\"Greenfield\") manufacturing facility located at 2750 Industrial Canal Road, Belle Chasse, Louisiana 70037, in Plaquemines Parish. The retention was made at the direction of Pinnacle in connection with Claim File CLM-2025-07744, involving Policy Nos. PNN-CP-2025-04891 and PNN-PLL-2025-06237.
34	
35	The scope of Vector\'s investigation includes the following:
36	
37	1\. Determine the root cause and mechanism of the Tank 7 structural failure that occurred on March 14, 2025.
38	
39	2\. Assess the sequence of events from the initial structural failure of Tank 7 through the subsequent chemical release, fire, and explosion.
40	
41	3\. Evaluate the condition and maintenance history of Tank 7, including review of available inspection records, maintenance logs, design drawings, and fabrication records.
42	
43	4\. Identify contributing factors to the failure, including material degradation mechanisms, operational conditions, and inspection and maintenance practices.
44	
45	5\. Assess the scope and extent of physical damage to adjacent structures, equipment, and infrastructure resulting from the incident.
46	
47	Vector\'s investigation was coordinated through Crossfield Adjusting Group, LLC, which served as the independent adjusting firm assigned to the claim. All document requests, site access coordination, and communications with Greenfield personnel during the investigation were facilitated through Crossfield.
48	
49	This report constitutes Vector\'s preliminary findings and conclusions. It is designated as preliminary because metallurgical laboratory analysis of recovered tank specimens is currently in progress and results are pending at the time of this report\'s issuance. A final report will be issued upon completion of the metallurgical analysis, incorporating laboratory findings and any revised or supplemental conclusions warranted by that analysis.
50	
51	**[Section 2 --- Background Information]{.underline}**
52	
53	Greenfield Specialty Chemicals, Inc. is a Louisiana corporation formed in 2009 and headquartered in Belle Chasse, Louisiana. The company manufactures specialty chemical intermediates used in the petrochemical and agricultural sectors. Greenfield\'s principal manufacturing operations are conducted at the Subject Facility located at 2750 Industrial Canal Road, Belle Chasse, Louisiana 70037, within Plaquemines Parish.
54	
55	The Subject Facility includes a tank farm containing multiple above-ground storage tanks, process buildings, pipe racks, electrical distribution infrastructure, and supporting utilities. The tank farm provides bulk storage for various chemical feedstocks and intermediates used in Greenfield\'s manufacturing processes.
56	
57	Tank 7 is a 50,000-gallon carbon steel above-ground storage tank that was used for the storage of methyldiethanolamine (\"MDEA\"), a liquid amine compound used in gas sweetening and acid gas treatment processes. At the time of the incident, Tank 7 contained approximately 38,000 gallons of MDEA. Tank 7 is situated within a secondary containment area consisting of a concrete-lined earthen berm designed to contain the full volume of the largest tank within the berm in the event of a release.
58	
59	Tank 6, an adjacent above-ground storage tank within the same containment area, contained approximately 25,000 gallons of monoethanolamine (\"MEA\") at the time of the incident. Tank 6 is located approximately 40 feet northwest of Tank 7.
60	
61	The incident that is the subject of this investigation occurred on March 14, 2025, at approximately 2:17 a.m. Central Standard Time. The incident resulted in the catastrophic structural failure of Tank 7, release of its contents, an arc flash event at an adjacent electrical junction box, and a subsequent fire and explosion that caused extensive damage to Tank 6, the pipe rack, electrical systems, and the adjacent processing building.
62	
63	The Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (\"LDEQ\") issued Compliance Order No. CO-2025-0341 on April 3, 2025, requiring Greenfield to undertake remediation of contaminated soil and groundwater resulting from the chemical release.
64	
65	**[Section 3 --- Investigation Methodology]{.underline}**
66	
67	Vector conducted on-site inspections of the Subject Facility on March 22--24, 2025, and April 8--9, 2025. The inspections were performed by Marcus D. Calloway, PE, CFEI, and Sandra L. Nguyen, PE. During the site inspections, Vector performed the following investigative activities:
68	
69	> • **Visual and Photographic Documentation.** Comprehensive visual examination and photographic documentation of the Tank 7 remains, Tank 6, the pipe rack, electrical Junction Box JB-14, electrical conduit and cabling in the tank farm area, and the adjacent processing building (north wall and roof). A total of 143 photographs were taken during the two site visits and are compiled in Appendix A to this report.
70	>
71	> • **Physical Specimen Collection.** Vector collected physical specimens from the failed Tank 7, including sections of the failed base ring weld seam, shell plates from the lowest shell course adjacent to the failure zone, and floor plate sections. These specimens were documented, labeled, and catalogued using chain-of-custody protocols. The specimens were submitted to an independent metallurgical laboratory for analysis, including fractography, metallographic examination, chemical composition analysis, and corrosion product characterization. Laboratory results are pending at the time of this report.
72	>
73	> • **Ultrasonic Thickness (UT) Measurements.** Vector performed ultrasonic thickness measurements on remaining intact sections of the Tank 7 shell that were recovered from the debris field. UT measurements were taken at multiple grid points to characterize the wall thickness profile in areas adjacent to and removed from the failure zone. UT measurement data is compiled in Appendix B.
74	>
75	> • **Document Review.** Vector reviewed the following documents as part of its investigation:
76	>
77	> • Tank 7 design drawings and fabrication records, as provided by Greenfield.
78	>
79	> • Greenfield\'s maintenance records for Tank 7 spanning the period from 2017 through 2025, including work orders, inspection logs, and maintenance schedules.
80	>
81	> • The external inspection report for Tank 7 prepared by Coastal Tank Inspection Services, LLC, dated June 12, 2023.
82	>
83	> • Greenfield\'s work order records, including the work order for the base ring exterior recoating completed on August 3, 2023.
84	>
85	> • LDEQ Compliance Order No. CO-2025-0341, issued April 3, 2025.
86	>
87	> • **Personnel Interviews.** Vector conducted interviews with Greenfield personnel, including Ray Fontenot, Maintenance Supervisor, who provided information regarding Tank 7\'s maintenance history, the August 2023 recoating work, and Greenfield\'s general tank inspection and maintenance program.
88	>
89	> • **Coordination with Crossfield Adjusting Group.** Vector coordinated with Crossfield Adjusting Group, LLC, regarding the overall damage assessment scope, access to documentation, and scheduling of site inspections.
90	
91	All physical specimens collected during the investigation have been submitted to the metallurgical laboratory for analysis, and the results of that analysis are pending at the time of issuance of this preliminary report.
92	
93	**[Section 4 --- Factual Findings]{.underline}**
94	
95	**Section 4.1 --- Sequence of Events**
96	
97	At approximately 2:17 a.m. Central Standard Time on March 14, 2025, Tank 7 at the Greenfield Specialty Chemicals, Inc. manufacturing facility suffered a catastrophic structural failure originating at the base ring area of the tank. The failure was abrupt and occurred without prior warning. There were no alarms triggered before the failure event, no visible precursors such as weeping, seepage, or bulging of the tank shell, and no gradual loss of tank contents preceding the rupture. Greenfield personnel who were on-site during the night shift reported hearing a single loud percussive event, described as a sudden, explosive sound, followed immediately by the sound of a large volume of liquid being released.
98	
99	The structural failure resulted in the rapid and uncontrolled release of approximately 38,000 gallons of methyldiethanolamine (\"MDEA\") from Tank 7. The liquid MDEA discharged from the failed base ring area and flowed across the concrete-lined secondary containment area surrounding the tank farm. The released MDEA flowed in a generally southeastern direction from Tank 7 and contacted electrical Junction Box JB-14, a pad-mounted electrical distribution junction box located approximately 35 feet southeast of Tank 7. Contact between the MDEA liquid and the energized electrical components within Junction Box JB-14 caused an arc flash event.
100	
101	The arc flash ignited MDEA vapors and liquid present in the immediate vicinity of Junction Box JB-14. The resulting fire spread rapidly across the surface of the released MDEA within the containment area and extended to adjacent structures and equipment. The fire engulfed Tank 6, which contained approximately 25,000 gallons of monoethanolamine (\"MEA\"), as well as the pipe rack connecting the tank farm to the main processing building. Electrical conduit runs routed along and adjacent to the pipe rack were also consumed by the fire. The fire caused structural damage and significant heat exposure to the north wall and roof of the processing building.
102	
103	The fire burned for approximately 4.5 hours before being brought under control by the Plaquemines Parish Fire Department, which responded to the scene, in coordination with Greenfield\'s on-site emergency response team. During the fire suppression efforts, firewater runoff contributed to the spread of MDEA-contaminated water beyond the secondary containment berm through a drain valve that had been compromised during the event.
104	
105	The catastrophic failure of Tank 7 was a sudden, abrupt event. The rupture occurred instantaneously, without any observable period of gradual deterioration, progressive leaking, or incremental loss of structural integrity immediately preceding the failure. The single percussive event reported by on-site personnel is consistent with a sudden through-wall fracture of the tank shell at the base ring, followed by immediate structural collapse and release of contents.
106	
107	**Section 4.2 --- Root Cause Analysis --- Tank 7 Failure Mechanism**
108	
109	Vector\'s examination of the Tank 7 remains identified the origin of the structural failure at a circumferential weld seam at the junction of the tank\'s lowest shell course and the base (annular) ring, on the interior side of the tank. The fracture propagated circumferentially along the weld seam, extending approximately 270 degrees around the tank\'s circumference, resulting in the near-complete separation of the lowest shell course from the annular ring and the catastrophic loss of structural integrity.
110	
111	Visual examination of the fracture surfaces revealed extensive internal corrosion along the interior surface of the weld seam and the adjacent heat-affected zone (\"HAZ\"). The corrosion morphology observed at the fracture surfaces includes localized pitting, undercutting along the weld toe, and cracking patterns that are consistent with microbiologically influenced corrosion (\"MIC\") and/or amine-induced stress corrosion cracking (\"SCC\"). Both MIC and SCC are well-documented degradation mechanisms in carbon steel equipment exposed to amine solutions such as MDEA. MIC is driven by the metabolic activity of sulfate-reducing bacteria and other microorganisms that can colonize wetted metal surfaces, particularly in stagnant or low-flow areas such as the base ring junction. SCC in amine service is associated with residual welding stresses in the HAZ combined with the electrochemical environment created by the amine solution. Both mechanisms produce corrosion and cracking that initiates on the interior (product-wetted) surface and propagates through the wall thickness.
112	
113	Ultrasonic thickness measurements performed on recovered shell sections adjacent to the failure zone revealed wall thicknesses as low as 0.087 inches in the most severely corroded areas, compared to the original nominal wall thickness of 0.375 inches as specified in the Tank 7 fabrication records. This represents a loss of approximately 77% of the original wall thickness in the affected area. UT measurements taken at locations removed from the failure zone showed wall thicknesses ranging from 0.310 to 0.355 inches, indicating that the severe wall thinning was localized to the base ring weld seam area on the interior surface rather than generalized across the tank shell.
114	
115	The corrosion was localized to the interior surface of the weld seam at the base ring junction. This location is submerged beneath the stored MDEA during normal tank operations and is situated at the lowest point of the tank interior, where sediment, water, and microbial accumulation are most likely to occur. The internal corrosion was not visible from external inspection of the tank. External visual examination of the tank shell, including the base ring area, would not reveal internal corrosion of this nature, as the corrosion initiated and propagated from the product-side surface inward through the wall thickness.
116	
117	Based on the observed corrosion depth, the morphology of the corrosion products, and typical propagation rates documented in the technical literature for MIC and SCC in carbon steel amine service, Vector estimates that the internal corrosion developed over a period of approximately 3 to 5 years. This estimate is preliminary and will be refined upon completion of the metallurgical laboratory analysis, which will include corrosion rate calculations based on metallographic cross-sections and corrosion product characterization.
118	
119	The progressive wall thinning caused by the internal corrosion ultimately reduced the remaining wall thickness at the base ring weld seam to a point where the metal could no longer sustain the hydrostatic pressure exerted by the approximately 38,000 gallons of stored MDEA. At the point of critical wall thinning, a through-wall fracture initiated and propagated rapidly around the circumference of the weld seam, resulting in the catastrophic structural failure observed on March 14, 2025. The failure event itself --- the through-wall fracture and structural rupture --- was abrupt, sudden, and instantaneous in nature. While the underlying corrosion mechanism developed gradually over a multi-year period, the structural failure occurred as a single, discrete event without any period of gradual leakage or progressive loss of contents preceding the rupture.
120	
121	**Section 4.3 --- Comparison with June 2023 External Inspection**
122	
123	As part of its investigation, Vector reviewed the external inspection report for Tank 7 prepared by Coastal Tank Inspection Services, LLC (\"Coastal Tank\"), dated June 12, 2023. The 2023 Coastal Tank report was prepared following an external inspection of Tank 7 and documented findings related to the tank\'s external condition. The report rated Tank 7\'s overall shell condition as \"satisfactory\" and noted \"minor surface corrosion at the base ring --- recommend monitoring at next scheduled inspection.\"
124	
125	Vector\'s investigation determined that the external surface corrosion noted in the 2023 Coastal Tank inspection report is a separate and distinct condition from the internal weld seam corrosion that caused the March 14, 2025, catastrophic failure of Tank 7. The two conditions differ in their location, their corrosion mechanism, and their severity, and they are not related as a matter of engineering analysis.
126	
127	The external surface corrosion identified in the 2023 Coastal Tank report was superficial oxidation on the exterior painted surface of the base ring plate. This type of surface corrosion is a common and expected condition for above-ground storage tanks operating in the humid southeastern Louisiana environment, where atmospheric moisture, salt air, and temperature cycling promote surface oxidation of painted carbon steel surfaces. The 2023 report described this condition as \"minor\" and recommended monitoring --- not immediate repair, not further investigation, and not an internal inspection. The external surface corrosion was located on the external surface of the base ring plate, visible from the outside of the tank, and it affected the paint coating and the outermost surface of the steel substrate.
128	
129	Greenfield\'s maintenance records confirm that, in direct response to the 2023 Coastal Tank inspection recommendation, a recoating of the base ring exterior was completed on August 3, 2023, under a maintenance work order supervised by Ray Fontenot, Greenfield\'s Maintenance Supervisor. This maintenance action was responsive, timely, and consistent with the recommendation made in the 2023 inspection report.
130	
131	The internal weld seam corrosion that caused the catastrophic failure of Tank 7 on March 14, 2025, was located on the interior (product-side) surface of the circumferential weld joining the lowest shell course to the annular ring. This location is on the inside of the tank, submerged beneath the stored MDEA during normal operations. It is accessible only during an internal inspection, which requires the tank to be taken out of service, emptied of all product, cleaned, gas-freed, and entered as a confined space by qualified inspection personnel. The internal corrosion mechanism --- MIC and/or amine-induced SCC --- is fundamentally different from the atmospheric surface oxidation observed externally. The internal corrosion was driven by the interaction of the carbon steel weld and HAZ with the stored MDEA product and associated microbial or electrochemical activity, not by atmospheric exposure.
132	
133	There is no indication that the internal corrosion condition that caused the failure was detectable through the routine external inspection methods employed during the 2023 Coastal Tank inspection, including visual inspection of the tank exterior, magnetic particle testing of external welds, or external ultrasonic thickness measurements. The internal corrosion was located on a surface that is inaccessible from the exterior of the tank while the tank is in service and containing product. External UT measurements, even if taken at the base ring location, measure wall thickness from the outside surface and may not reliably detect localized internal pitting or weld-toe undercutting in the specific geometry of the shell-to-annular-ring weld junction, particularly if the corrosion is concentrated at the weld toe on the interior surface.
134	
135	In summary, the external surface corrosion identified in the 2023 Coastal Tank inspection report and the internal weld seam corrosion that caused the 2025 tank failure are two separate and distinct conditions, differing in location, mechanism, and severity. The 2023 inspection identified only the external condition. Greenfield remediated the external condition promptly.
136	
137	**Section 4.4 --- Assessment of Maintenance Practices**
138	
139	Vector reviewed Greenfield\'s tank inspection and maintenance program for Tank 7, including maintenance records, work orders, inspection schedules, and related documentation spanning the period from 2017 through 2025.
140	
141	Greenfield\'s tank inspection program is structured in accordance with API Standard 653, *Tank Inspection, Repair, Alteration, and Reconstruction* (\"API 653\"), which is the recognized industry standard governing the inspection, repair, and integrity management of above-ground storage tanks after they have been placed in service. API 653 is published by the American Petroleum Institute and is widely adopted throughout the petrochemical, chemical, and energy industries as the standard of care for tank integrity management programs. Compliance with API 653 is generally regarded as constituting adherence to industry-standard practices for tank maintenance and inspection.
142	
143	Tank 7\'s external inspection history, as documented in the records reviewed by Vector, shows that external inspections were conducted at regular intervals consistent with API 653 requirements. API 653 prescribes external inspection intervals that typically do not exceed five years for tanks in satisfactory condition, with the interval adjusted based on the tank\'s condition, service history, and corrosion rate data. The most recent external inspection of Tank 7, conducted on June 12, 2023, by Coastal Tank Inspection Services, LLC, was performed within the applicable API 653 external inspection interval. The 2023 inspection rated the tank\'s overall condition as \"satisfactory.\"
144	
145	Greenfield\'s maintenance records further demonstrate that maintenance actions were taken in response to inspection findings. As discussed in Section 4.3 above, the August 3, 2023, base ring exterior recoating was performed in direct response to the recommendation in the 2023 Coastal Tank inspection report. This is consistent with a responsive maintenance program that addresses identified conditions in a timely manner.
146	
147	With respect to internal inspections, API 653 establishes internal inspection intervals based on corrosion rate data and remaining wall thickness calculations. For tanks in satisfactory condition for which internal corrosion rate data is not available --- because internal corrosion rate data can only be obtained through an internal inspection --- API 653 provides guidance for establishing an initial internal inspection interval. The standard generally contemplates internal inspection intervals not exceeding 10 years, or a calculated interval based on dividing one-half of the remaining corrosion allowance by the measured or estimated corrosion rate, whichever yields a shorter interval. For a tank rated in satisfactory external condition with no known internal corrosion issues and no available internal corrosion rate data, a 5- to 10-year internal inspection cycle is consistent with API 653 guidance.
148	
149	The records reviewed by Vector do not identify the date of Tank 7\'s most recent internal inspection. However, the 2023 Coastal Tank external inspection report\'s notation of \"minor surface corrosion\" at the base ring does not, under API 653, trigger a mandatory immediate internal inspection. API 653 recognizes that minor external surface corrosion is a maintenance condition to be addressed through protective coating repair and monitoring, which is the action that Greenfield undertook. A finding of minor external surface corrosion is not an indicator of internal corrosion, and API 653 does not require an internal inspection based solely on such a finding. The standard distinguishes between conditions that warrant enhanced monitoring or coating repair (such as minor external surface corrosion) and conditions that would trigger an immediate or accelerated internal inspection (such as evidence of shell distortion, active leaking, or significant wall thinning detected by external UT measurements).
150	
151	Based on its review of Greenfield\'s maintenance records, inspection reports, and related documentation, Vector did not identify any specific deficiency in Greenfield\'s inspection or maintenance practices for Tank 7 that would constitute a deviation from industry-standard tank integrity management practices as established by API 653. Greenfield maintained a documented inspection program, conducted external inspections at appropriate intervals, and took responsive maintenance action in accordance with inspection recommendations.
152	
153	**[Section 5 --- Damage Assessment Summary]{.underline}**
154	
155	Vector\'s site inspections documented the following damage resulting from the March 14, 2025, incident:
156	
157	**Tank 7.** Total loss. Tank 7 suffered catastrophic structural failure at the base ring weld seam, resulting in near-complete separation of the lowest shell course from the annular ring and collapse of the tank structure. The tank is not repairable and requires full demolition and replacement.
158	
159	**Tank 6.** Tank 6, located approximately 40 feet northwest of Tank 7, sustained significant fire and thermal damage. Shell plates on the side facing Tank 7 exhibited warping and deformation from prolonged heat exposure. The internal lining of Tank 6 was compromised by thermal degradation. Tank 6 requires full replacement.
160	
161	**Pipe Rack.** The pipe rack connecting the tank farm to the main processing building sustained severe fire damage. Structural steel members showed deformation, buckling, and loss of protective coating from direct flame impingement and radiant heat exposure. Pipe supports were compromised, and piping within the rack sustained thermal damage. The pipe rack requires full demolition and reconstruction.
162	
163	**Electrical Systems.** Junction Box JB-14 was destroyed by the arc flash event and subsequent fire. It was the origin point of the ignition. Approximately 1,200 linear feet of electrical conduit and cabling in the tank farm and pipe rack area sustained fire damage rendering the systems non-functional. Full replacement of the affected electrical distribution infrastructure is required.
164	
165	**Processing Building.** The north wall and roof of the processing building sustained heat, smoke, and soot damage from radiant and convective thermal exposure. Structural steel framing in the north bay shows measurable deflection from thermal exposure, indicating temperatures sufficient to reduce the yield strength of the structural members. Interior process equipment located in the north bay of the processing building sustained smoke contamination and water damage from fire suppression activities.
166	
167	**Damage Causation.** It is noted that the majority of the physical damage to structures and equipment other than Tank 7 itself was caused by the fire and thermal exposure resulting from the ignition of MDEA vapors and liquid following the arc flash at Junction Box JB-14. Direct damage attributable to contact with the released MDEA liquid was limited to the tank farm secondary containment berm area, the soil beneath and surrounding Tank 7, and Junction Box JB-14 itself. The fire damage extended significantly beyond the area of direct MDEA contact and constituted the principal cause of damage to Tank 6, the pipe rack, the electrical conduit systems, and the processing building.
168	
169	**Environmental Impact.** Approximately 38,000 gallons of MDEA were released onto the ground surface within the tank farm secondary containment area. A portion of the released MDEA migrated beyond the secondary containment berm through a drain valve that was compromised during the incident, resulting in confirmed soil and shallow groundwater contamination in the area surrounding the containment berm. Environmental assessment and remediation are being addressed under LDEQ Compliance Order No. CO-2025-0341. Vector defers to Redfield Environmental Consulting, LLC, and other qualified environmental specialists for the scope and cost of environmental remediation.
170	
171	Damage cost estimates and repair/replacement cost quantification are outside the scope of this forensic engineering investigation. Vector defers to Crossfield Adjusting Group, LLC, and to Greenfield\'s contractor, Acadian Industrial Constructors, for cost quantification.
172	
173	**[Section 6 --- Preliminary Conclusions]{.underline}**
174	
175	Based on the investigation performed to date, including site inspections, physical evidence examination, ultrasonic thickness measurements, document review, and personnel interviews, Vector offers the following preliminary conclusions:
176	
177	1\. The catastrophic failure of Tank 7 on March 14, 2025, was caused by through-wall corrosion at the interior circumferential weld seam joining the lowest shell course to the annular (base) ring. The corrosion progressively reduced the wall thickness at the weld seam until the remaining metal could no longer sustain the hydrostatic pressure of the stored MDEA, resulting in a through-wall fracture and structural rupture.
178	
179	2\. The corrosion morphology observed at the failure zone is consistent with microbiologically influenced corrosion (\"MIC\") and/or amine-induced stress corrosion cracking (\"SCC\"), both of which are recognized degradation mechanisms associated with carbon steel in amine service. Metallurgical laboratory analysis of recovered specimens is pending and is expected to confirm the specific corrosion mechanism.
180	
181	3\. The internal corrosion developed over an estimated period of approximately 3 to 5 years, progressively reducing the wall thickness from the original nominal thickness of 0.375 inches to as low as 0.087 inches at the point of failure --- representing a loss of approximately 77% of the original wall thickness at the most severely corroded location.
182	
183	4\. The tank failure was abrupt and catastrophic, occurring without observable precursors such as weeping, seepage, bulging, or alarm activation. On-site personnel reported a single percussive event consistent with a sudden structural rupture. The failure event itself was instantaneous.
184	
185	5\. The internal weld seam corrosion that caused the failure was located on the product-side (interior) surface of the tank, submerged beneath the stored MDEA during normal operations. This corrosion was not visible or detectable through routine external inspection methods, including visual inspection, magnetic particle testing, or external ultrasonic thickness measurements.
186	
187	6\. The external surface corrosion noted in the June 12, 2023, Coastal Tank Inspection Services, LLC, external inspection report is a separate and distinct condition from the internal weld seam corrosion that caused the failure. The two conditions differ in location (exterior surface vs. interior surface), mechanism (atmospheric oxidation vs. MIC/SCC), and severity (minor surface corrosion vs. 77% wall thickness loss). The 2023 inspection report identified only the external surface condition and rated the tank\'s overall condition as \"satisfactory.\"
188	
189	7\. Greenfield\'s response to the 2023 inspection finding --- completion of a base ring exterior recoating on August 3, 2023 --- was appropriate, timely, and consistent with the recommendation contained in the 2023 inspection report.
190	
191	8\. Greenfield\'s tank inspection and maintenance program, as documented in the records reviewed by Vector, is structured in accordance with API 653, *Tank Inspection, Repair, Alteration, and Reconstruction*, which is the recognized industry standard for above-ground storage tank integrity management. External inspections were conducted at intervals consistent with API 653 requirements. Maintenance actions were taken in response to inspection findings. Vector did not identify any specific deficiency in Greenfield\'s inspection or maintenance practices that would constitute a departure from recognized industry standards for above-ground storage tank integrity management.
192	
193	9\. The released MDEA contacted electrical Junction Box JB-14, located approximately 35 feet southeast of Tank 7, producing an arc flash that ignited MDEA vapors and liquid and initiated a fire. The fire spread to Tank 6, the pipe rack, electrical conduit systems, and the adjacent processing building, causing the majority of the observed property damage to structures and equipment other than Tank 7 itself. Direct damage from MDEA contact was limited principally to the tank farm containment area, surrounding soil, and Junction Box JB-14.
194	
195	**[Section 7 --- Limitations and Qualifications]{.underline}**
196	
197	This is a preliminary report. The conclusions and opinions expressed herein are subject to revision upon completion of the metallurgical laboratory analysis of recovered specimens from Tank 7. The final report will incorporate laboratory findings and any revised, supplemental, or additional conclusions warranted by that analysis. Laboratory results are expected within approximately 4 to 6 weeks of the date of this report.
198	
199	Conclusions regarding the specific corrosion mechanism (MIC vs. SCC) are preliminary and based on visual and macroscopic examination of fracture surfaces and corrosion morphology observed during site inspections. Laboratory confirmation through metallographic examination, fractography, chemical composition analysis, and corrosion product characterization is pending.
200	
201	The estimated corrosion timeline of approximately 3 to 5 years is based on the observed corrosion depth, the morphology of the corroded surfaces, and typical propagation rates documented in the published technical literature for MIC and SCC in carbon steel amine service. The actual timeline of corrosion development may vary from this estimate, and the metallurgical laboratory analysis may provide additional data to refine or adjust this estimate.
202	
203	Vector did not independently verify all of Greenfield\'s maintenance records and relied in part on records and representations provided by Greenfield and its personnel during the investigation. Vector has no reason to believe the records provided were incomplete or inaccurate, but this reliance is noted as a qualification to the conclusions presented herein.
204	
205	Damage cost estimates, repair and replacement cost quantification, and business interruption assessments are outside the scope of this forensic engineering investigation. Vector defers to Crossfield Adjusting Group, LLC, and to Greenfield\'s contractor, Acadian Industrial Constructors, for cost quantification and scope of repair.
206	
207	Environmental assessment, remediation scope, and remediation cost estimation are outside the scope of Vector\'s engagement. Vector defers to Redfield Environmental Consulting, LLC, and to the requirements of LDEQ Compliance Order No. CO-2025-0341 for environmental remediation matters.
208	
209	**[Section 8 --- Signature Block and Certifications]{.underline}**
210	
211	This report has been prepared for the sole use of Pinnacle Assurance Corporation in connection with Claim File CLM-2025-07744. Distribution to third parties without the express written consent of Vector Engineering Solutions, LLC, is not authorized. The findings, opinions, and conclusions expressed in this report are based on the investigation performed to date and are subject to revision as described in Section 7 above.
212	
213	VECTOR ENGINEERING SOLUTIONS, LLC
